report.summary: Both failures are one product bug: the server accepts a book whose year is next year (2027), but the test suite and the app's own error message require it to be rejected. The validator in app/main.py:83 uses `this_year + 1` as the upper bound, while the message on line 84 says 'between 1 and {this_year}'. Fix the bound in app/main.py first; both tests should then pass without changes.

causes.title: Year validation accepts next year (off-by-one upper bound)
causes.explanation: validate_book() allows years up to this_year + 1, so a book dated next year is saved with status 201 instead of being rejected with 422. The API test expects that rejection, and the UI test expects the 'Year must be between' error and no saved row. In the UI run the book was saved as 'Future-d41404e1 Someone 2027', so no error element appeared. The validator is also inconsistent with its own message, which says the range ends at this year. Test test_current_year_is_accepted (year = THIS_YEAR) still passes, so the boundary that is wrong is exactly the one the two failing tests exercise. The behaviour is deterministic for any run in the current year, so this is not flakiness. I did not have git history to confirm whether the +1 was added on purpose; the message and the tests both indicate it is a bug.
evidence: app/main.py:84: raise HTTPException(422, f"Year must be between 1 and {this_year}")
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:42-44: books.add(title, "Someone", str(date.today().year + 1)); expect(books.error).to_contain_text("Year must be between")
UI failure: 'Error: element(s) not found' for get_by_test_id("error"); aria snapshot shows row "Future-d41404e1 Someone 2027" was saved
causes.suggested_fix: In app/main.py:83 change `this_year + 1` to `this_year` so the condition is `if not 1 <= book.year <= this_year:`. Then confirm that the message on line 84 and the tests agree, and rerun both failing tests plus test_current_year_is_accepted. If next-year books were meant to be allowed, the fix goes the other way: update the test expectations and the error message instead.
